mn87:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn87:2.1: Now on that occasion a certain householder’s dear and beloved only son had died.
mn87:2.2: After his son’s death, he gave no more thought to his work or his meals.
mn87:2.3: He kept going to the charnel-ground and crying:
mn87:2.4: ‘My only child, where are you? My only child, where are you?’
mn87:3.1: Then he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the Blessed One said to him:
mn87:3.2: ‘Householder, your faculties seem those one of who is out of his mind. Your faculties are in no normal state.’
mn87:3.3: ‘How should my faculties be in their normal state, venerable sir?
mn87:3.4: For my dear and beloved only son is dead.
mn87:3.5: Since he died I have given no more thought to my work or my meals.
mn87:3.6: I keep going to the charnel ground and crying:
mn87:3.7: “My only child, where are you? My only child, where are you?”’
mn87:3.8: ‘So it is, householder, so it is.
mn87:3.9: Dear ones, those who are dear (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.’
mn87:3.11: dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair?
mn87:3.12: Venerable sir, dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) happiness and joy.’
mn87:3.13: Then, not delighting in the Blessed One’s words, and disapproving, he got up from his seat and went away.
mn87:4.1: Now on that occasion some gamblers were playing with dice not far from the Blessed One.
mn87:4.2: Then the householder went to the gamblers and said:
mn87:4.3: ‘Just now, sirs, I went to the monk Gotama, and after paying homage to him, I sat down at one side. When he had done so, the monk Gotama asked me:
mn87:4.4: “Householder, your faculties seem those of one who is out of his mind. Your faculties are not in their normal state.”
mn87:4.5: When that was said, sirs, I told him:
mn87:4.6: “How should my faculties be in their normal-state, venerable sir?
mn87:4.7: For my dear and beloved only son is dead.
mn87:4.8: Since he died I have thought no more about my work and my meals.
mn87:4.9: I keep going to the charnel ground and crying:
mn87:4.10: ‘My only child, where are you? My only child, where are you?’ “
mn87:4.11: (But he told me) “So it is, householder, so it is.
mn87:4.12: Dear ones, those who are dear (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.”
mn87:4.13: (I said) “Venerable sir, who would ever (think) that
mn87:4.14: dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair?
mn87:4.15: Venerable sir, dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) happiness and joy.”
mn87:4.16: Then not delighting in the monk Gotama’s words, and disapproving, I got up from my seat and went away.’
mn87:4.17: ‘So it is, householder, so it is.
mn87:4.18: Dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) happiness and joy.’
mn87:4.19: Then the householder (thought:) ‘I agree with the gamblers.’ And he went away.
mn87:5.1: That story eventually reached the king’s palace.
mn87:5.2: King Pasenadi of Kosala told Queen Mallikā:
mn87:5.3: ‘This is what has been said by the monk Gotama, Mallikā:
mn87:5.4: “Dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair”.’
mn87:5.5: ‘If that has been said by the Blessed One, sire, then that is so.’
mn87:5.6: ‘No matter what the monk Gotama says, thus Mallikā applauds it:
mn87:5.7: “If that has been said by the Blessed One, sire, then that is so” (she says,)
mn87:5.8: just like a pupil who applauds, no matter what his teacher says to him:
mn87:5.9: “So it is, teacher, so it is”,
mn87:5.10: and so too, Mallikā, no matter what the monk Gotama says, you applaud it:
mn87:5.11: “If that has been said by the Blessed One sire, then that is so.”
mn87:5.12: Be off, Mallikā; away with you!’
mn87:6.1: Then Queen Mallikā told Nalijangha of the divine caste:
mn87:6.2: ‘Come, divine, go to the Blessed One and pay homage in my name with your head at his feet, and ask whether he is free from affliction, free from ailment and is healthy, strong and living in comfort,
mn87:6.3: (saying:) “Venerable sir, Queen Mallikā pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet, and she asks whether the Blessed One is free from affliction, free from ailment, and is healthy, strong and living in comfort,
mn87:6.5: ‘Venerable sir, have these words been uttered by the Blessed One:
mn87:6.6: “Dear ones, those who are dear (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair”?’
mn87:6.7: Learn well what the Blessed One replied and tell it me;
mn87:6.9: ‘Yes, madam,’ he replied; and he went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him,
mn87:6.10: and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn87:6.11: ‘Master Gotama, Queen Mallikā pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet and asks whether the Blessed One is free from affliction, free from ailment, and is healthy, strong and living in comfort;
mn87:6.13: “Venerable sir, have these words been spoken by the Blessed One:
mn87:6.14: ‘Dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair’?”’
mn87:7.1: ‘So it is, divine, so it is.
mn87:7.2: Dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.
mn87:8.1: ‘And it can be understood from this how dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair:
mn87:8.2: Once in this same Sāvatthi there was a certain woman whose mother died.
mn87:8.3: Owing to her (mother’s) death she lost her mind, and wandered mad from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads, saying:
mn87:8.4: “Have you seen my mother ? Have you seen my mother ?”
mn87:9-14.1: ‘And it can also be understood from this how dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair:
mn87:9-14.2: Once in this same Sāvatthi there was a certain woman whose father died …
mn87:9-14.8: Owing to her (husband’s) death she went mad, out of her mind, and she wandered from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads, saying:
mn87:9-14.9: “Have you seen my husband? Have you seen my husband?”

mn87:22.1: Once in this same Sāvatthi there was a woman who married and went to live in her husband’s family.
mn87:22.2: Her relatives wanted to divorce her from her husband and give her to another
mn87:22.4: Then the woman said to her husband:
mn87:22.5: “Lord, these relatives of mine want to divorce me from you and give me to another
mn87:22.7: Then the man cut the woman in two and himself committed suicide, thinking:
mn87:22.9: It can also be understood from this how dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.’
mn87:23.1: Then delighting in the Blessed One’s words and agreeing, the divine-caste Nalijangha got up from his seat and went to Queen Mallikā to whom he recounted the whole of his conversation with the Blessed One. Then Queen Mallikā went to King Pasenadi of Kosala and asked him:
mn87:24.2: is Princess Vajiri dear to you ?’
mn87:24.3: ‘Yes Mallikā, Princess Vajiri is dear to me.’
mn87:24.5: if change and alteration took place in Princess Vajiri (would that bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair?’
mn87:24.6: ‘A change and alteration in Princess Vajiri would mean an alteration in my life. How could sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair not arise in me?’
mn87:24.7: ‘It was was with reference to that, sire, that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:
mn87:24.8: “Dear ones, those who are dear, (bring) sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.”’

mn87:29.1: ‘It is wonderful, Mallikā, it is marvellous
mn87:29.2: how far the Blessed One penetrates with understanding and sees with understanding!
mn87:29.3: Come, Mallikā, give me the ablution water.’
mn87:29.4: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala got up from his seat, and arranging his upper robe on one shoulder, he raised his hands palms together towards where the Blessed One was, and he uttered this exclamation three times:
mn87:29.5: ‘Honour to the Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened!
mn87:29.6: Honour to the Blessed One, Arahant and Fully Enlightened!
